title: Longest Common Substring
statement: You are given two lowercase strings a and b. A substring is a run of characters that appears contiguously (no gaps). Return the length of the longest string that is a substring of BOTH a and b. If the two strings share no character at all, return 0. Because you want a contiguous match, this differs from a subsequence: 'abcde' and 'axcye' share only single letters contiguously, so the answer is 1, even though a, c, and e all appear in order in both.
hints: You need a match that is contiguous in both strings, so ask: what is the longest common run that ends exactly at a[i-1] and b[j-1]?

Let dp[i][j] be the length of the longest common suffix of a[:i] and b[:j]. On a character match it extends the diagonal by 1; on a mismatch it is 0, not a carry-over. The answer is the maximum cell, not dp[m][n].
Fill an (m+1) by (n+1) grid of zeros. For each i, j: if a[i-1] == b[j-1] set dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + 1 and update a running best; otherwise leave dp[i][j] at 0. Return best.
